query_state.description: Query power/color state. Frame: 81 8A 8B <checksum>. Reply begins 0x81 (modern) or 0x66 (original).

set_color.description: Set RGB(W) color (8-byte form): 31 RR GG BB WW <write_mode> 0F <checksum>. write_mode selects RGB vs white channel handling (0xF0 RGB-only, 0x0F white-only, 0xFF both) per flux_led.

methods.notes: Discovery in practice is the Hi-Flying module's UDP 48899 config channel: broadcast the ASCII "HF-A11ASSISTHREAD", to which modules answer "+ok" and then report IP/MAC/model. See zengge_lan_protocol.

device.manufacturer: Zengge (white-labeled: Magic Home, Magic Hue, MagicLight, Flux, and dozens more)
device.name: Magic Home / Zengge Wi-Fi LED Controller
device.notes:
Zengge makes the Wi-Fi LED controllers and bulbs sold under a huge number of brands — Magic Home, Magic Hue, MagicLight, Flux and many more. They speak a plaintext binary protocol on TCP port 5577 with NO authentication and no handshake. flux_led reverse-engineered it from packet captures and is the client Home Assistant uses. Zengge is still in business (manufacturer_status active), but the local protocol is what matters here: block the controller from the internet and everything below still works.
TRANSPORT: TCP 5577, binary commands. The last byte of every command is a checksum = (sum of all preceding bytes) & 0xFF. Several protocol variants exist — the original (no checksum), an 8-byte and a 9-byte color form, and addressable A1/A2/A3 strip protocols; the newest (A3/CCT/Christmas) wrap the inner command in an outer frame beginning B0 B1 B2 B3 00 01.
KEY COMMANDS (from flux_led protocol.py):
  power on  : 71 23 0F + checksum
  power off : 71 24 0F + checksum
  state query: 81 8A 8B + checksum  (reply begins 0x81 on modern protocols,
               0x66 on the original checksum-less one)
  color set : 31 RR GG BB WW <write_mode> 0F + checksum (8-byte form; a
               9-byte form adds a second/cool white byte)
  device config query (addressable): 63 ... returns LED count, segments,
               IC type (WS2812B/SK6812/...) and wiring order.

HARDWARE: legacy units are Hi-Flying HF-LPB100/LPT120 modules; newer ones are ESP8285-based.

openness.notes: No vendor documentation; the protocol was reverse-engineered from packet captures. flux_led (now under the lightinglibs org) is the authoritative implementation and backs Home Assistant's flux_led integration.

credentials.notes: The home passphrase is sent as an AT-style command over the UDP 48899 config channel — no encryption. Post-setup TCP 5577 control is unauthenticated: anything on the LAN can drive the controller.

factory_reset.effect: Returns the module to AP/setup mode and clears Wi-Fi credentials. Per-controller reset gestures (power-cycle sequences) are not documented in the sources used here.

methods.description: Join the module's setup AP and drive the UDP 48899 config channel: send "HF-A11ASSISTHREAD", wait for "+ok", then set the home SSID and passphrase with the module's AT-style commands. The module reboots onto the home network and answers on TCP 5577.

steps.action: Power a new/reset controller and join its setup AP.
Send the AT-style commands that set the home SSID/passphrase.
steps.expect: The module reboots and joins the home Wi-Fi; TCP 5577 answers.

setup.notes: A factory-fresh module hosts its own AP; joining it to the home Wi-Fi uses the Hi-Flying UDP 48899 config channel (ASCII AT-style commands set the SSID and passphrase after the HF-A11ASSISTHREAD handshake). No cloud account is needed for local control. The exact AT sequence is not replayed here — low.

rejoin.notes: The UDP 48899 config channel can rewrite the module's Wi-Fi credentials without a physical reset when the module is reachable.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Command bytes, the port-5577 transport and the additive checksum are transcribed from flux_led's protocol.py and vikstrous/zengge-lightcontrol.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only. Control is binary over a raw TCP socket on port 5577 (see zengge_lan_protocol); discovery is over UDP 48899. There is no HTTP control surface on most modules (some expose a status page on port 80).

zengge_lan_protocol.cloud_note: Cloud path (not needed locally): bulbs tunnel to wifi.magichue.net:8805, AES256 with a shared secret. Local TCP 5577 is wholly independent of it.

control.checksum: last byte = (sum of all preceding bytes) & 0xFF
control.variants: original (no checksum), 8-byte color, 9-byte color (adds cool white), and addressable A1/A2/A3 strip protocols. The newest (A3/CCT/Christmas) wrap the inner command in an outer frame beginning B0 B1 B2 B3 00 01.

discovery.handshake: Broadcast ASCII 'HF-A11ASSISTHREAD'; module answers '+ok', then reports IP/MAC/model. Same channel configures the home SSID/passphrase.
